title: The agency spectrum
point: Pick the lowest level of agency that meets the requirement, because each level up adds cost, latency and failure modes.
definition: The agency spectrum ranks systems from level 0, a fixed pipeline, to level 5, an open-ended supervised agent. Each level hands the model one more kind of decision.

objective.text: Given six product requirements, choose the lowest sufficient agency level for each and justify the choice by naming the decision the next level up would add.

misconceptions.claim: Higher levels are more advanced, so they make the better default.
misconceptions.correction: Higher levels cost more and are harder to test. The right default is the lowest level that meets the requirement, raised only when a measured gap demands it.

misconceptions.claim: A router and a tool caller are the same thing.
misconceptions.correction: A router picks among fixed branches and passes no arguments. A tool caller also constructs arguments, which opens a new failure mode: inputs that look valid but are wrong.

l1: Level 0 is a fixed pipeline where code decides every step. Level 1 is a router: the model picks one branch from a fixed set. Level 2 is a tool caller: the model picks a tool and its arguments, once.
Level 3 is a bounded loop of choose, act and observe. Level 4 is a planner and executor that writes and revises a multi-step plan. Level 5 is open-ended work under human supervision.
The point to remember: pick the lowest level that meets the requirement, because every level up adds cost, latency and failure modes.
l2: A travel company wants to answer the question of where a booking is. The answer needs one lookup by booking reference, so a level 2 tool caller is enough. The model extracts the reference and calls the lookup once.

The same company also wants to rebook missed connections across airlines. The next search depends on the seat availability seen in the previous one, so that task needs at least a level 3 bounded loop.
Same company, two requirements, two levels. The level follows the requirement, not the team's ambition.
l3: Suppose a level 2 design resolves 88 per cent of requests and a level 3 loop resolves 94 per cent at three times the cost per request.
Running level 3 on everything pays triple cost on all hundred requests to rescue six. A cheaper hybrid runs level 2 first and invokes level 3 only on the 12 per cent it cannot resolve.
That hybrid adds roughly 12 per cent times three, about 36 per cent, to average cost instead of 200 per cent. State that number when you defend the design.
